items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: We were almost supposed to do something with him with that. I wish we had had the chance.

ctx.x: was Ray Brown, Ed Thigpen and myself. And we were teaching there. And I got a call from Verve records and they said, “we would like you to do something on ‘West Side Story.’” And I said, oh, boy, I’d heard some of the score and that’s not easy, you know. So they said, “could you put something together and we’d like to do it soon, because the show is hot, and we’d like to get it out.” You know like record companies, it’s like do it yesterday. So while we were teaching, on off periods, I would call the group…
Oh, yes. Tenderness, fire, and beauty. I know that the composer, Bernstein, I know he loved it. I know he loved it you know. To hear his music interpreted like that.
We were almost supposed to do something with him with that. I wish we had had the chance.
